 BREAKING Wolverhampton Wanderers Darts legend Michael van Gerwen on target at Wolves training ground
 By Matt Maher Chief sports writer
 Comment Published 21st Nov 2026, 04:01 GMT The three-time world champion visited the club this week.
 Darts legend Michael van Gerwen was right on target when he took on a trio of Wolves players.
 The Dutch hero is through to the quarter-finals of the Grand Slam of Darts after beating James Wade at Aldersley Leisure Village on Thursday night.

And Van Gerwen warmed-up for the clash by taking a trip to Compton Park to face Wolves stars Adam Armstrong, Tommy Doyle and John Ruddy on the oche.
 All three players had been in the crowd at Aldersley earlier in the week to watch him progress through the group stage of the tournament.
 Ruddy, playing off 301 while Van Gerwen played from 501, came close to snatching the first leg of a best-of-three match only to stumble on the doubles.
 Armstrong and Doyle then teamed up to no avail as the three-time world champion showed his class.
 “We had a few fun games here with the players – as always these days, it’s all about the content!” said Van Gerwen. 
 “But it’s nice to be here. I’ve never been here to the training ground before, I’ve been to the stadium before but not here, and it was a pleasure to be here.
 “John came close, but I was never worried because getting close doesn’t count. You have to hit the doubles and do the right things at the right moments. That’s what matters.
 “But Adam’s a decent player. He probably needed a warm-up, but luckily for me, he didn’t have one, otherwise I could have been in trouble!”
